findings.evidence: R-19 (weight-based quorum over the door's signer list) + R-21 (weight >= quorum finalizes) + R-43 (model): a forged event backed by colluding weight at or above quorum finalizes and moves funds to the attacker's destination. The code header states it directly: 'if a quorum of them collude, they can steal the funds put into trust' (E01).
findings.title: Quorum collusion steals the door's funds: colluding witness weight at or above quorum finalizes a forged event

findings.evidence: R-24 (no minimum witness count in bridge code; ledger minimum is 1 signer, STTx.h:53-64) + scenario S-07: a 1-of-1 bridge is creatable, and its single witness reaching quorum alone is total loss.
findings.title: No minimum witness count: a 1-of-1 bridge is creatable and one compromised witness is total loss

findings.evidence: R-40 (absence: no signer-list or master-key check in the bridge-creation path, XChainBridge.cpp:1374-1545; probe I-01) + R-15 (an enabled master key is accepted for attestations) + scenario S-06 run B: a door whose master key was never disabled can be drained without any witness.
findings.title: Door master-key disablement is not enforced in code: bridge creation never checks the door's master key or signer list

findings.evidence: R-44 (model) + threshold table: with 8 witnesses and quorum 5, 4 colluding witnesses leave honest weight 4 below quorum 5, so neither side finalizes; the same holds at 32 witnesses with quorum 17.
findings.title: Even witness count with majority quorum degrades at maximum safe collusion instead of staying safe

findings.evidence: R-18 (attestations from removed signers are erased) + R-26 (signer-list change uses the new set) + scenario S-05 run B: removing 3 of 5 witnesses mid-claim drops live weight to 2, below quorum 3, and the claim cannot recover without a signer-list change.
findings.title: Signer-list churn can strand a claim: attestations from removed signers are erased on the next quorum count

findings.evidence: R-17 (re-attestation replaces the old attestation) + R-22 (match is on amount, chain direction, and destination): a witness can switch its attested amount or destination by re-attesting, and the new attestation replaces the old one instead of adding to it.
findings.title: Re-attestation replaces: a witness can change its attested amount or destination by attesting again

findings.evidence: E06 (finalizeClaimHelper: if reward distribution fails, the main transfer is rolled back; for keepClaim claims the claim is kept) + scenario S-11: if the claim owner spent the reward funds between commit and claim, finalize fails tecUNFUNDED_PAYMENT and the claim is kept for a retry.
findings.title: An unfunded reward pool stalls a claim: the main transfer rolls back and the claim is kept for a retry

findings.evidence: R-33 (failed account-create transfer removes the claim; claimCount still advances, 'Move past this claim id even if it fails', E14): on a non-UNFUNDED, non-INTERNAL finalize failure the claim is consumed while no account is created and no funds move; the committed funds stay in the door with no code path to reclaim them through that claim.
findings.title: An account-create failure consumes the claim: the count advances even when no account is created

findings.evidence: R-38 (a quorum must agree on the SignatureReward) + E37 (the account-create signed message carries the reward amount) + E14 (the account-create reward paid is the triggering attestation's value, attBegin->rewardAmount): the paid reward is whatever the triggering attestation claims, so a quorum agreeing on an inflated reward drains the door beyond the bridge's stated SignatureReward.
findings.title: The account-create reward paid is the triggering attestation's value, not the bridge's SignatureReward

findings.evidence: R-22 (match fields) + absence grep: AttestationRewardAccount never appears in XChainBridge.cpp (probe I-01), so no check constrains the reward account to be the signer or a listed account; per-account reward failures other than UNFUNDED or INTERNAL are tolerated and the distribution continues.
findings.title: The reward account is unconstrained: any account can be named, and a per-account failure is tolerated

findings.evidence: R-45 (absence: no expiry field or check exists on claim IDs; probe I-01) + R-28 (claim IDs are destroyed only when funds move): a stale claim can be completed at any later time.
findings.title: Claim IDs never expire: a stale claim can be completed at any later time

findings.evidence: R-37 (equal split with downward rounding when fixXChainRewardRounding is enabled, E07) + the distributed > rewardPool guard: the undistributed remainder stays with the reward pool source.
findings.title: Reward rounding leaves a remainder with the reward pool source
